paragraphs.text: He declares that their words which would diminish anything from the justice of God, are but as a puff of wind that vanishes away.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: That is, has rewarded them according to their iniquity, meaning that Job should be warned by the example of his children, that he not offend God.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: That is, if you turn while God calls you to repentance.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: Though the beginning is not as pleasant as you would like, yet in the end you will have sufficient opportunity to please yourself.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: He wills Job to examine all antiquity and he will find it true which he here says.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Meaning, that it is not enough to have the experience of ourselves, but to be confirmed by the examples of those who went before us.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: As a rush cannot grow without moisture, so the hypocrite because he does not have faith which is watered with God's Spirit.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Which is today and tomorrow swept away.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: He compares the just to a tree, which although it is moved from one place to another, yet flourishes: so the affliction of the godly turns to their profit.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: That is, so that there remains nothing there to prove whether the tree had grown there or not.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: To be planted in another place, where it may grow as it pleases.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: If you are godly, he will give you opportunity to rejoice and if not your affliction will increase.
paragraphs.label: m
